text: RGTI is down 55% on your position and 75% from its high with negative earnings, heavy insider selling, and 18% short interest — the thesis is broken and holding this is just hoping, not investing.
QBTS is down 44% and 64% off its high with no earnings, insiders dumping shares, and 20% short interest — this has all the hallmarks of a broken speculative position and should be sold.

IONQ is down 35% on your position and 60% from its high with cash burn, insider selling, and 13% short interest — in a stagflationary macro environment, unprofitable companies with this much damage get worse, not better.

NCLP.L is your worst-performing holding by percentage at minus 22% and 34% off its high — consider trimming to reduce concentrated loss risk, especially with weakening consumer spending in the macro outlook.
ARCI.L is a large holding down 31.6% from its 52-week high, which is an unusually deep drawdown for an ETF — trim the oversized position to manage risk while the macro picture remains uncertain.

ServiceNow is down 50% from its high but growing revenue at 21% with strong free cash flow — that's a rare pullback in a proven business, and a small add here at this level makes sense if you can stomach near-term volatility.
Google is down 20% from its high at a PE of 21.6 with 15% revenue growth and insider buying — that's a quality large-cap on sale, worth adding to gradually at these levels.
